subject: Amendment request: adding 16-GPU burst pool + revised reserved hourly
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@dataforge.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: DataForge Procurement <procurement@dataforge.ai>
Date: 2027-10-03T09:12:00Z
Subject: Capacity ask ahead of renewal

Matt (and team),

As we approach our November renewal, we ran a set of load tests and want to discuss a firm plan to go from our current 16-GPU reserved pool to a 32-GPU baseline. Two important asks from our side: a) a clear change to reserved per-hour pricing for the expanded commit, and b) a throughput guarantee (p95 token latency) for our burst and steady-state traffic patterns.

Wed like to understand options: immediate 32-GPU commit vs staged approach with a 16-GPU reserved pool plus a 16-GPU burst pool for the first quarter after renewal. Also attaching the draft SOW and our perf summary. Can you propose a practical amendment we can circulate to procurement?

Thanks,
Emma Jones
VP, Platform Engineering
DataForge

Attachments: DataForge_SOW_draft_v3.pdf, perf_summary_q3.xlsx

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@dataforge.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-03T13:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Capacity ask ahead of renewal

Emma — thanks for the clear ask and the perf artifacts. High level response below, then Ill follow with a concise amendment draft for procurement.

Summary proposals (options):
- Option A (Immediate commit): Convert to a firm 32-GPU reserved pool for the 12-month renewal. New per-hour reserved rate: see attached pricing_table_16to32.xlsx; headline: 12% reduction on the incremental 16 GPUs vs current hourly list. SLA: 99.9% uptime; throughput target: p95 token latency under 150ms for <1k concurrent requests (model-dependent).
- Option B (Staircase with burst pool): Keep 16-GPU reserved baseline, add a 16-GPU dedicated burst pool for the first 90 days post-renewal. Reserved per-hour for baseline unchanged; burst pool billed at a reduced reserved incremental rate (intro credit applied) for the first quarter. After 90 days, we transition to a full 32-GPU reserved commit at the agreed incremental hourly. This reduces up-front cost and lets us validate traffic.
- Option C (Hybrid with throughput SLAs): 16-GPU reserve + 16-GPU on-demand with guaranteed pre-warmed capacity windows (we reserve slots for your traffic peaks). This is more operationally flexible but has slightly higher unit cost.

Next steps: Ill loop legal/procurement language into a short amendment: term, incremental hourly, transition mechanics, and a rollback/fallback in case performance regressions appear. For procurement, Option B tends to be easiest to operationalize. Thoughts?

— Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_table_16to32.xlsx

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-04T10:22:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Capacity ask ahead of renewal — internal pricing note

Mateo — quick internal: procurement will push on headline per-hour for the incremental 16 GPUs. If we go Option B (staircase), we can offer a 10% intro credit on the burst pool for 90 days (applied as one-off invoice credit) and lock-in the longer-term incremental hourly at a 9% discount to list if they convert to full 32 within the first 6 months. That keeps net effective price close to a straight 32 commit but with lower cash hit up front. Also recommend including a 30-day SLA review clause and automatic fallback to the prior model if perf falls outside agreed limits.

Laura Bennett
Director, Commercial Operations

On pricing_table_16to32.xlsx: see row "staircase_intro_credit"

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@dataforge.ai>, DataForge Procurement <procurement@dataforge.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-05T15:08:00Z
Subject: Draft amendment and proposed commercial terms (DataForge renewal)

Emma — attached is a short amendment we can sign to operationalize Option B (Staircase with Burst Pool). Key commercial bullets are below and mirrored in the attached PDF/SOW: 

1) Term & baseline: 12-month renewal effective 2027-11-01; baseline reserved commit remains 16 GPUs for months 1-3.
2) Burst pool: a 16-GPU dedicated burst pool (same instance class) active for days 1-90 post-renewal. Burst pool billed at an introductory incremental reserved rate of $X.XX/hr per GPU (10% credit applied off the incremental list).
3) Conversion path: If DataForge signs conversion to full 32-GPU reserved within 180 days, incremental hourly rate for the converted GPUs will be locked at a 9% discount to list and the 90-day credits will be credited back as agreed.
4) Throughput & SLA: We guarantee p95 generation latency <150ms for your validated workload within the 16+burst configuration for steady-state forecasts up to 1k concurrent requests. If we fail the SLA for 3 consecutive weekly checks, well provide a service credit and immediate ops escalation.
4) Ops runbook: pre-warm windows for scheduled peak hours, automated KV/prefix caching retention during transition, and a 24x7 escalation hook to our Dedicated Infra team.

If this looks good, we can convert the amendment into procurement language and route for signatures. Im happy to hop on a 20-minute call with procurement today to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
+1 415 555 0198

Attachments: DataForge_SOW_draft_v3.pdf, pricing_table_16to32.xlsx

From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@dataforge.ai>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: DataForge Procurement <procurement@dataforge.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-05T16:47:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft amendment and proposed commercial terms (DataForge renewal)

Thanks, Mateo — this is helpful and close to what we discussed. A couple of procurement asks: please replace the vague "$X.XX/hr" with concrete hourly numbers and include a line item that shows blended effective hourly across months 1-6 for our finance reviewers. Also request clearer failure remediation SLAs (whats the credit percentage and TTR). Procurement copied here; well get back with redlines by end of day Thursday. Can you share a short spreadsheet with the line-item math (blended hours / credits) so we can circulate internally?

Ill schedule a 20-minute call if we need to walk through. Appreciate the speedy turnaround.

Emma
VP, Platform Engineering, DataForge
